practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 124(1) of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice of India and, until Parliament by law prescribes a larger number, of not more than seven other Judges.

practiceQuestions.q: Who administers the oath of office to the Chief Justice of India?
opts: The Minister of Law and Justice
The outgoing Chief Justice of India
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 124(6), every person appointed to be a Judge of the Supreme Court shall, before he enters upon his office, make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed in that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out in the Third Schedule.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the retirement age of the Chief Justice of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: As per Article 124(2), a Judge of the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice, holds office until they attain the age of 65 years.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the first Chief Justice of independent India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Justice Harilal Jekisundas Kania (H. J. Kania) served as the first Chief Justice of India from January 26, 1950, until his death in 1951.

practiceQuestions.q: Under which constitutional provision can the President appoint an ad hoc judge to the Supreme Court, with the previous consent of the Chief Justice of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 127 provides for the appointment of ad hoc judges. If at any time there should not be a quorum of the Judges of the Supreme Court available to hold or continue any session of the Court, the CJI may, with the previous consent of the President and in consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned, request in writing the attendance of a High Court judge qualified to be a Supreme Court judge.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary role of the Chief Justice of India in the administrative setup of the Supreme Court?
practiceQuestions.sol: The CJI is designated as the 'Master of the Roster', meaning they possess the prerogative to constitute benches and assign cases to various judges of the Supreme Court.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article deals with the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice of India when the office of CJI is vacant or when the CJI is unable to perform their duties?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 126 of the Constitution deals with the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice. When the office of Chief Justice of India is vacant or when the Chief Justice is, by reason of absence or otherwise, unable to perform the duties of their office, the duties of the office shall be performed by such one of the other judges of the Court as the President may appoint for the purpose.

practiceQuestions.q: Who determines the salaries, allowances, leave of absence, and pension of the Supreme Court judges, including the Chief Justice?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 125 of the Constitution provides that Parliament shall determine by law the salaries, allowances, leave of absence, and pension of the Supreme Court judges.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies recommends the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Collegium system, headed by the Chief Justice of India and consisting of the four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court, is responsible for the appointment and transfer of judges.

practiceQuestions.q: Where is the seat of the Supreme Court of India located, though the Constitution provides that the CJI can appoint other places as well with the approval of the President?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 130 states that the Supreme Court shall sit in Delhi or in such other place or places as the Chief Justice of India may, with the approval of the President, from time to time, appoint.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the appointment mechanism of the Chief Justice of India evolve from the plain text of the Constitution to the current judicial consensus?
opts: It has always been decided solely by a vote in Lok Sabha.
From absolute executive discretion to judicial primacy established through the 'Three Judges Cases', leading to the Collegium system.
From recommendation by the Prime Minister to direct election by High Court judges.
From control by the Attorney General to selection by the Law Commission.
practiceQuestions.sol: Initially, Article 124(2) gave the President the power to appoint the CJI after consultation with judges. Through the First, Second, and Third Judges Cases (1981, 1993, 1998), the Supreme Court interpreted 'consultation' as 'concurrence', giving primacy to the judiciary and giving birth to the Collegium system for appointments.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the convention traditionally followed regarding the appointment of the Chief Justice of India, and how was it departed from?
opts: Appointment of the senior-most judge; departed in 1973 and 1977.
Rotation among High Court Chief Justices; departed in 2000.
Nomination by the Law Minister; never departed.
practiceQuestions.sol: Convention dictates that the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court should be appointed as the CJI. This convention was superseded in 1973 when Justice A.N. Ray was appointed superseding three senior judges, and again in 1977 when Justice M.H. Beg was appointed superseding Justice H.R. Khanna.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Constitution prohibit a person who has held office as a Judge of the Supreme Court, including the CJI, from pleading or acting in any court or before any authority within the territory of India?
opts: To reduce the workload of lower courts.
To ensure absolute judicial independence and impartiality without post-retirement temptations or conflicts of interest.
To encourage them to move abroad for international arbitration.
To enable them to enter active politics immediately.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 124(7) bars retired SC judges from practicing law in India. This post-retirement restriction safeguards judicial independence, ensuring judges do not lean toward executive favor while in office with an eye on post-retirement legal practices.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional significance of the CJI's role in the impeachment process of a judge?
opts: The CJI single-handedly removes any judge through an executive order.
Under the Judges Inquiry Act, the CJI nominates a 3-member committee to investigate charges against a judge whose removal is sought.
The CJI casts the final decisive vote in Parliament during impeachment.
The CJI has no role; impeachment is purely legislative.
practiceQuestions.sol: While the removal of a Supreme Court judge is governed by Article 124(4) and the Judges Inquiry Act, 1968, if the motion is against a Supreme Court judge, the inquiry committee constituted by the Speaker/Chairman includes a Supreme Court judge nominated by the CJI. If the inquiry is against the CJI himself, the committee includes a Chief Justice of a High Court.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the CJI exercise administrative control over the listing of Public Interest Litigations (PILs)?
opts: By acting as the Master of the Roster, deciding which bench hears urgent PILs and suo motu matters.
By consulting the Law Minister directly on every PIL file
By delegating all PIL assignments exclusively to the Attorney General
practiceQuestions.sol: As the 'Master of the Roster', the CJI has the exclusive authority to allocate cases, including PILs and suo motu cognizance matters, to specific benches, ensuring systemic management of judicial caseloads.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of Article 143 in relation to the Chief Justice of India?
opts: It empowers the CJI to issue executive ordinances.
It governs the President's power to consult the Supreme Court, where the CJI presides over the advisory bench.
It allows the CJI to transfer cases from High Courts to lower courts.
It deals with the contempt powers of the Supreme Court.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 143 provides the President with advisory jurisdiction to consult the Supreme Court on questions of law or fact. When such a reference is made, the CJI constitutes a bench (usually a Constitution Bench of at least 5 judges) to render an advisory opinion to the President.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are Constitution Benches convened, and what is the role of the CJI in forming them?
opts: They are convened for ordinary bail applications, formed automatically by the Law Ministry.
They decide substantial questions of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution (at least 5 judges), and are formed solely by the CJI as Master of the Roster.
They hear tax disputes of corporate entities, appointed by the Prime Minister.
They review administrative orders of the Supreme Court Registry, appointed by the Registrar.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 145(3), cases involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution must be heard by a bench of at least five judges. The CJI exercises absolute administrative discretion in constituting these benches.

practiceQuestions.q: What constitutional protection ensures that the conduct of Supreme Court judges, including the CJI, cannot be discussed in Parliament except upon a motion for impeachment?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 121 prohibits discussion in Parliament with respect to the conduct of any judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of their duties, except in the case of an impeachment motion under Article 124(4).

practiceQuestions.q: How does the CJI play a role in the appointment of High Court judges and Chief Justices?
opts: The CJI appoints them unilaterally without consulting anyone.
Through the Supreme Court Collegium, which recommends names for High Court appointments in consultation with senior-most SC judges and consultee judges.
The CJI has no say in High Court appointments; it is done by State Governors.
Through direct orders to the Chief Ministers.
practiceQuestions.sol: The SC Collegium, headed by the CJI and comprising two senior-most judges, recommends appointments and transfers of High Court judges and Chief Justices, which are then processed by the Ministry of Law and Justice for presidential approval.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the 'In-House Procedure' developed by the Supreme Court under the CJI?
opts: It is a mechanism to impeach judges in Parliament.
It is an internal peer-review mechanism led by the CJI to examine complaints of judicial misconduct against judges without resorting to formal impeachment immediately.
It manages the financial budget of the Supreme Court.
It recruits administrative staff for courtrooms.
practiceQuestions.sol: The In-House Procedure was formulated by the Supreme Court to address judicial misconduct internally. If a complaint is received against a judge, the CJI constitutes a committee of Chief Justices and judges to investigate, preserving institutional integrity while dealing with ethical lapses.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Justice of India:
1. The Constitution of India prescribes a specific minimum age qualification for appointment as a Supreme Court judge or Chief Justice.
2. The administrative expenses of the Supreme Court, including all salaries and allowances of the CJI and judges, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Constitution does not prescribe any minimum age for appointment as a Supreme Court judge. Statement 2 is correct; Article 146(3) and Article 112(3)(d) specify that administrative expenses and salaries of Supreme Court judges are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India, making them non-votable in Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of the Chief Justice of India:
1. Article 124 of the Constitution explicitly mentions the term 'Collegium'.
2. The Second Judges Case (1993) ruled that the recommendation made by the CJI without consulting the two senior-most judges is not binding on the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; the term 'Collegium' does not appear anywhere in the original text of the Constitution; it is a judicial innovation born out of Supreme Court judgments. Statement 2 is correct: the Second Judges Case established that the CJI must consult a collegium of senior judges, and a solo recommendation by the CJI lacks concurrence and is not binding.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers and functions of the CJI:
1. The CJI has the sole administrative power to allocate cases and establish benches as the Master of the Roster.
2. The CJI can unilaterally alter the retirement age of Supreme Court judges through administrative circulars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; the CJI is recognized as the Master of the Roster with exclusive case allocation authority. Statement 2 is incorrect because the retirement age of Supreme Court judges is fixed at 65 years by Article 124(2) of the Constitution and can only be amended by a constitutional amendment enacted by Parliament, not by judicial circulars.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of a Supreme Court Judge or Chief Justice:
1. A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed from office by an order of the President passed after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority.
2. The grounds for removal specified in the Constitution are 'proved misbehaviour' or 'incapacity'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under Article 124(4), an address supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting is required, along with presidential assent, on the grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Acting Chief Justice and Ad Hoc judges:
1. Article 126 empowers the President to appoint an Acting Chief Justice of India.
2. Ad hoc judges appointed under Article 127 must be qualified to be appointed as judges of the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate. Article 126 provides for Acting CJI appointment by the President when the office is vacant or the CJI is absent. Article 127 specifies that an ad hoc judge drawn from a High Court must be duly qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative independence of the Supreme Court under the CJI:
1. The CJI appoints all officers and servants of the Supreme Court, and their conditions of service are determined by the CJI or an officer authorized by them.
2. Such rules made by the CJI regarding staff conditions do not require the approval of the President of India under any circumstances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Article 146(1) vests appointment power in the CJI. Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 146(2) explicitly states that rules relating to salaries, allowances, leave, or pensions of officers and servants of the Supreme Court require the approval of the President.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the transfer of High Court judges involving the CJI:
1. The CJI can recommend the transfer of a judge from one High Court to another only after consulting a collegium consisting of the four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court and the Chief Justices of the two concerned High Courts.
2. The consent of the transferred judge is mandatory for such transfers to take effect.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Article 222 empowers the President to transfer a judge after consultation with the CJI, which, per the Third Judges Case, requires the CJI to consult the collegium and relevant High Court Chief Justices. Statement 2 is incorrect: as per the Third Judges Case, transfer of High Court judges does not require the judge's consent, and judicial transfer is a punitive/administrative prerogative of the collegium.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the retirement and post-retirement engagements of the Chief Justice of India:
1. The Constitution completely bars retired Supreme Court judges, including the CJI, from being appointed to any tribunal, commission, or public office under the government.
2. Several former Chief Justices of India have been appointed to constitutional offices such as Governors or Chairpersons of statutory bodies like the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Constitution only bars them from pleading or acting in courts (Article 124(7)); it does not explicitly bar them from taking up executive appointments like tribunals, commissions, or governorships (though it remains a subject of intense debate regarding judicial independence). Statement 2 is correct as several former CJIs have taken up such roles post-retirement.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the evolution of the Collegium system for appointing the CJI and Supreme Court judges:
1. In the First Judges Case (1981), the Supreme Court held that 'consultation' with the CJI meant 'concurrence', giving absolute veto power to the judiciary.
2. The National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) Act, 2014, was struck down by the Supreme Court as unconstitutional because it violated the Basic Structure doctrine by undermining judicial independence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; the First Judges Case (SP Gupta case, 1981) held that 'consultation' did not mean 'concurrence' and gave primacy to the executive in judicial appointments. Concurrence was established later in the Second Judges Case (1993). Statement 2 is correct: the Fourth Judges Case (2015) struck down the NJAC Act, ruling that executive involvement in judicial appointments violated the independence of the judiciary, a basic feature of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional position of the Chief Justice of India:
1. The CJI has the power to assign PIL petitions to specific benches, and this administrative power is immune from judicial review under all circumstances.
2. The Chief Justice of India can initiate suo motu proceedings based on news reports, letters, or representations without formal petitions being filed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because recent judgments (such as Shanti Bhushan v. Supreme Court of India) have clarified aspects of the Master of the Roster, and administrative actions of the CJI are subject to scrutiny on grounds of arbitrariness or mala fides, though they carry high presumption of regularity. Statement 2 is correct; the Supreme Court under the CJI exercises expansive epistemic jurisdiction, taking up suo motu cognizance on the basis of letters, media reports, and telegrams in matters of public importance and human rights violations.
